Meanwhile, spot Ethereum ETFs recorded a total net outflow of $29.09 million yesterday, marking their third consecutive day of net outflows. — link

Binance Plans to Enter Five Asian Markets Next Year, Focusing on South and Southeast Asia According to Reuters, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker said the company plans to enter five Asian markets next year, focusing on South and Southeast Asia. It is in talks with five or six markets, with three at an advanced stage. The markets were not named; details are expected in the first quarter of next year. Following a $6.3 billion crypto theft last month, Binance contacted regulators in Japan, South Korea, Australia, Thailand and New Zealand within 36 to 48 hours. Seker said discussions with regulators on industry-wide security threats are ongoing. — link

Ledger Users Report Losses From Dubai-Bought Wallets After Teardown Reveals Suspected Hardware Implant According to The Defiant, two users reported crypto thefts from Ledger hardware wallets allegedly bought at official reseller Virgin Megastore in Dubai: account Rewinsky reported losing ~1,300 SOL on Nov. 15, and internal photos of their Ledger Flex were confirmed by Mark Karpelès’ public OSINT registry to contain an added circuit board and antenna matching implants previously found in Southeast Asia. The second account, New Babylon Order, claimed 507,000 USDT was stolen on Nov. 14 from a Ledger Stax bought in October, though it remains unconfirmed without internal photos. Such physical implants capture recovery phrases displayed during setup over cellular networks without altering the secure element—allowing tampered units to pass Ledger’s Genuine Check—while the reported purchase channels remain unverified and Ledger has not confirmed related drains outside Southeast Asia. — link

Highlight Clip: CZ: Entrepreneurs Still Building in Crypto Are More Worth Investing in Amid the AI Boom CZ: Entrepreneurs Still Building in Crypto Are More Worth Investing in Amid the AI Boom Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said during the closing fireside chat at Cantor Convergence on November 12 that AI companies are creating tremendous value and deserve high valuations, but the industry also has a bubble. He believes 99% of today's AI startups will eventually fail, similar to the ICO and IEO boom in crypto. As attention shifts toward AI, entrepreneurs still building in crypto are more solid, making it easier to identify investment opportunities. CZ added that AI will not replace money or the internet but will use both and require more capital. He is now more bullish on crypto than ever. — link
